newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan Ag see average crop output.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan Ag see average crop output.

text.p: Preliminary crop yield estimates for Saskatchewan's crop indicated an average output, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its crop report.

Crop output was forecast to reach 24.2 million tonnes, almost eight percent above the 10-year average but 13 percent below 1996 production. The above average output was due to a 10 percent increase in harvested area but an average yield potential for most crops except wheat, durum and canola which will be below average.
Warm, dry weather with scattered rainfall lead to the cautious yield estimate.
Crop reporters said output could improve on normal temperatures and rainfall.

Rainfall was seen throughout the central and northern grainbelt as well as the southeast. Severe hail and wind storms were reported across Saskatchewan with the most significant damage reported around Kamsack on July 25.

The southern grainbelt saw hot and dry weather with measurable amounts of rainfall in the east. Crop growth was ahead of normal due to warm, dry conditions. Spraying of wheat midge was finished while spraying of Diamondback moths and Bertha armyworms on canola began.

Central Saskatchewan saw dry and hot weather in the west central region with moderate temperatures and frequent showers in the east. Crop growth continued to gain on the season. Spraying of wheat midge was finished while spraying of Diamondback moths and Bertha armyworms on canola began.

Northern grainbelt crops were rated in good to excellent conditions except in the northwest. Crop growth advanced at a normal pace. Spraying of wheat midge was finished while spraying of Diamondback moths and Bertha armyworms on canola began.
